sasha: Quick heads-up — after last week's kernel-selection rollout I'm seeing our internal cost-per-unit estimate diverge from billing by ~12%. Looks like per-token accounting on the dashboard doesn't match chargeback numbers. Anyone else seeing this?
kevin: I noticed higher token latency in the new kernels, which could affect token accounting windows. Do you have an example model/route?
sasha: route=/api/v1/generate model=redwood-7b-quant v2. Billing says $0.0124/token-equivalent but dashboard unit-econ shows $0.0109. Profile shows more time in "post-attn" kernels.
maria: @sasha can you paste the profiler snippet? also, are we including KV cache fill ops in the token counts? Those were toggled on in the rollout.
sasha: pasted short trace: ```
[profile] 2026-03-10T14:21Z route=/api/v1/generate
tokens=1024 total_ms=420
kernel.attn.forward ms=120
kernel.attn.backward ms=0
kernel.post_attn ms=160
kernel.kv_write ms=45
batching.overhead ms=25
network / serialization ms=70
```
kevin: hmm post_attn 160ms is big. Could be new fused kernel selecting a slower path for 1024 seq lengths. That would inflate per-token CPU/GPU time but billing uses token bytes only. We need to reconcile.
maria: I think two things: 1) our telemetry (flightdeck) counts "tokens_processed" as tokens emitted, but cost model multiplies by average serving GPU-time-per-token. If kernel selection changed latency-per-token but our per-token-time metric wasn't updated, that mismatch yields the percent delta. 2) KV write ops are currently charged to route as separate line-item in billing but our dashboard aggregates them into tokens.
kevin: Proposed quick checks: - run A/B on the kernel selector with a small sample and compute actual GPU-ms-per-token via nvtx/prof - update dashboard metric to show GPU-ms/token and billing-aligned "billable_token_equiv" metric - add KV-op counter as separate series.
sasha: Agreed. I ran a small perf job earlier: ```
# quick script to compute ms/token from traces
samples=50
for run in $(seq $samples); do cat /tmp/trace_$run.json | jq '.events | map(select(.name=="kernel_time")) | add / .tokens'; done | awk '{sum+= $1} END {print sum/NR}'
# result ~0.412 ms/token for new kernel vs 0.355 old
```
maria: that delta matches ~16% runtime increase which explains the cost gap. Good find.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployed kernel-selector v2 to 10% of hosts at 2026-03-10T01:04:23Z
kevin: For dashboards: I suggest a new per-route panel layout: - top row: tokens/sec, avg GPU-ms/token, p50/p95 token latency (breakdown: kernel, batching, network) - second row: billable_token_equiv (derived from billing formula), cost_per_minute, predicted_charge_error% - third row: kernel-selector variant split + KV-op rate.
maria: Also add an alert: when predicted_charge_error% > 5% for 30m, page infra oncall. This keeps finance from being surprised.
sasha: Who owns the metric "avg GPU-ms/token"? Is that infra team or runtime? I can add a short exporter PR if needed.
kevin: runtime infra should own the exporter (it has access to nvml/nvprof). I can own the dashboard and the derived "billable_token_equiv" query.
maria: I'll file a quick RFC for the accounting change so finance signs off on the billable_token_equiv formula. We need to be explicit about KV ops and quantization multipliers.
sasha: Action items: 1) kevin: dashboard + alerts (ETA EOD) 2) runtime infra: exporter for GPU-ms/token (owner: kevin?) 3) maria: RFC for billing alignment 4) perf team: run A/B with kernel selector rollback option (owner: perf)
kevin: I'll start the dashboard draft and push the queries: example PromQLs - tokens: sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[5m])) by (route) - gpu_ms_per_token: sum(rate(gpu_ms_total[5m])) / sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[5m])) - billable_token_equiv: sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_write_ops[5m])) * kv_token_multiplier
sasha: perfect. I'll attach the sample traces to the RFC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
